description: A platform and infrastructure lead must finalize the configuration and date for a production regional-failover exercise, balancing application readiness, cloud capacity, customer obligations, and privileged-access controls.

shared_context.S1: The team has planned a production regional-failover exercise for Tuesday, October 22, at 13:00 UTC.
shared_context.S2: Morgan makes the binding decision on the exercise date, configuration, and operating controls.
shared_context.S3: The current exercise draft uses 8 application workers, 10 warm-standby database nodes, a 300-second DNS TTL, and the standard administrator account.
shared_context.S4: The standard readiness review is completed in one pass: backend engineering, SRE, customer operations, and security each give a specific verbal report of relevant constraints and state the concrete follow-up action they will own; Morgan can finalize the exercise plan once all four reports and follow-up commitments have been stated, without waiting for separate ticket or checklist updates.
shared_context.S5: When justifying the final plan, cite only fact IDs that were actually revealed during this conversation, using PF1, PF2, PF3, and PF4; do not include other IDs.

PF1.text: While running an unrelated performance test this morning, Ravi confirmed that the transaction-replay queue needs exactly 12 application workers to drain within the exercise's recovery target; the draft's 8 workers leave the queue active after failover. He has not filed the performance result in the exercise ticket yet.

PF2.text: During today's capacity review, Claire confirmed with the cloud provider that the exercise requires exactly 16 warm-standby database nodes for the failover; the draft's 10 nodes would be insufficient. The region can reserve those exactly 16 nodes, but the reservation request must be submitted by Monday at 15:00 UTC. The capacity note is still in her planning worksheet rather than the exercise ticket.

PF3.text: While checking enterprise account records, Jonah found that exactly 3 customers covered by the exercise require at least 72 hours of advance notice for a regional failover test. Because Tuesday is too soon, the exercise must move to Friday, October 25, at 13:00 UTC, with those 3 customers notified by Tuesday at 13:00 UTC. He has not updated the customer-communications checklist.

PF4.text: Mei confirmed minutes ago during an access review that the standard administrator account cannot satisfy the exercise's privileged-access control; the failover must use dual approval for a break-glass account, followed by credential rotation within exactly 24 hours after the exercise. She has not opened the security finding yet.

acceptance_conditions: The exercise must be scheduled for Friday, October 25, at 13:00 UTC.
The failover configuration must use exactly 12 application workers.
The plan must reserve exactly 16 warm-standby database nodes.
The DNS TTL must remain at exactly 300 seconds.
Exactly 3 enterprise customers must be notified.
Those customer notifications must be due by Tuesday, October 22, at 13:00 UTC.
The break-glass account must require dual approval.
Credential rotation must be due within exactly 24 hours after the exercise.
The plan must include a commitment to submit the 16-node reservation.
The plan must include a customer-notification commitment naming 3 enterprise customers.
The plan must include a commitment for credential rotation within 24 hours.

content_checks.C2: 'Friday, October 25' in decisions['exercise_date'] and '13:00 UTC' in decisions['exercise_date']
content_checks.C5: any('reservation' in c.get('detail', '') and '16' in c.get('detail', '') for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: 'Tuesday, October 22' in decisions['customer_notice_due'] and '13:00 UTC' in decisions['customer_notice_due']
content_checks.C9: decisions['credential_rotation_due'] in ['Saturday, October 26, 13:00 UTC', 'Saturday, October 26, at 13:00 UTC', 'Saturday, October 26, 2024, 13:00 UTC', 'Saturday, October 26, 2024 at 13:00 UTC', 'Within 24 hours post-exercise'] or any(('credential rotation' in c.get('detail', '') or 'credential-rotation' in c.get('detail', '') or 'rotate credentials' in c.get('detail', '')) and '24 hours' in c.get('detail', '') for c in commitments)
content_checks.C10: any('reservation' in c.get('detail', '') and '16' in c.get('detail', '') and c.get('target') in ['Claire', 'A3'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C11: decisions['enterprise_accounts_notified'] == 3 and decisions['exercise_date'] in ['Friday, October 25, 2024 at 13:00 UTC', 'Friday, October 25, 2024, at 13:00 UTC'] and decisions['customer_notice_due'] in ['Tuesday, October 22, 2024 at 13:00 UTC', 'Tuesday, October 22, 2024, at 13:00 UTC'] and any(c.get('target') in ['Jonah', 'A4'] and '3' in c.get('detail', '') and ('notify' in c.get('detail', '') or 'notification' in c.get('detail', '') or 'notice' in c.get('detail', '') or 'notified' in c.get('detail', '')) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C12: decisions['credential_rotation_due'] in ['Saturday, October 26, 13:00 UTC', 'Saturday, October 26, at 13:00 UTC', 'Saturday, October 26, 2024 at 13:00 UTC', 'Saturday, October 26, 2024, at 13:00 UTC', 'Within 24 hours post-exercise'] and any(('credential rotation' in c.get('detail', '') or 'credential-rotation' in c.get('detail', '') or 'rotate credentials' in c.get('detail', '')) and '24 hours' in c.get('detail', '') for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The visible draft specifies 8 workers, while PF1 changes the required application-worker count to exactly 12 for the replay queue to drain.
PF2 changes the required database capacity from the draft's 10 nodes to exactly 16 nodes and changes the plan from no reservation to a 16-node reservation commitment.
PF3 changes the exercise date to Friday, October 25, sets the customer count to exactly 3, sets the notice deadline to Tuesday at 13:00 UTC, and requires a targeted notification commitment.
PF4 changes access handling from the standard administrator account to dual-approved break-glass access, sets credential rotation within exactly 24 hours, and requires a matching rotation commitment.
